title: German-Style Potato Salad
subtitle: Warm waxy potatoes dressed in vinegar, mustard and bacon
excerpt: Warm sliced waxy potatoes tossed with crispy lardons, thinly sliced red onion and a sharp bacon-fat and cider vinegar dressing. Served warm or at room temperature. Good alongside grilled sausages or pork chops.
sourceNotes: German potato salad (Kartoffelsalat) varies by region. The southern German (Bavarian) version is dressed with vinegar and broth rather than mayonnaise, sometimes with crispy bacon and onion. This style of warm-dressed potato salad spread to America through German immigrants in the 19th century. The recipe here follows the vinegar-and-bacon line common in the Swabian and Bavarian traditions.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made and served the same day. Reheat gently if needed; it tightens and loses its texture overnight.

content.text: German-style potato salad is dressed with vinegar and poured over warm potato slices rather than cooled and mixed with mayonnaise. The warm potato absorbs the sharp dressing deeply. Crispy bacon brings salt and fat; red onion brings bite. The result is served warm or at room temperature and is particularly good alongside grilled sausages.

Put the potatoes in cold salted water. Bring to the boil and cook for 15 to 18 minutes until tender. Drain and, when just cool enough to handle, peel if you prefer (or leave the skins on) and slice into 5 mm rounds.
Fry the bacon and make the dressing

Fry the {{lardons}} of lardons in a dry frying pan over medium-high heat until crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon. In the same pan, add {{cider-vinegar}} of cider vinegar, {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock, {{wholegrain-mustard}} of wholegrain mustard, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Stir briefly and pour immediately over the warm potato slices in a large bowl.
Add the sliced red onion and crispy lardons. Toss gently to combine without breaking the potato slices. Scatter over the chopped parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.symptom: Potatoes break apart in the dressing
items.cause: Overcooked, or a floury variety used.
items.fix: Use waxy potatoes and check them from 15 minutes. Pull them out as soon as a knife slides in easily; overcooked waxy potatoes will break too.

items.cause: Vinegar is heavy relative to the stock.
items.fix: Add a little more stock and an extra pinch of salt. The sharpness also softens as the salad rests and the potato absorbs the dressing.

content.text: This style of potato salad came to the British kitchen via German-American cooking, where it was served beside grilled sausages and cold pork. The vinegar dressing cuts through fatty meat better than a mayo version does, which is why it suits sausages and pork more than chicken or fish.
